problems: The card says a literal backslash in the input is a problem on Windows. Nothing in the task, the commit message or the review says that. Only a decoded `\` (%5C) on Windows is unsafe. An engineer following the card may wrongly reject URLs that contain a raw backslash.

The card says a byte is unsafe if it is NUL or `/`, without saying this applies only to bytes produced by percent-decoding (%00, %2F). A literal `/` path separator must still be accepted. As worded, the card invites rejecting ordinary slashes.

The card leaves out the point the reviewer treated as blocking at PS12 ('Documentation is contradicted by code'): what happens to `appendTo` when the function fails. The code truncated or nulled `appendTo` in a way that did not match the docs when `appendTo` was not null beforehand. The fix is either to document that failure clears `appendTo` to a null QString, or to keep a `wasNull` flag (since `origSize` cannot tell empty from null) and restore it, or to document and `Q_PRE` that `appendTo` is null on entry. The engineer needs to make the failure-path contract for `appendTo` consistent with the documentation.
